# ramka for Svelte

> Unstyled, accessible lightbox primitives for Svelte — in the style of Radix UI and Base UI.

Generated from the HTML docs sources. Do not edit by hand — run `pnpm docs:llms`.

# Installation

Unstyled, accessible lightbox primitives for Svelte 5, in the style of Bits UI. Compose your own lightbox UI on headless parts with view-transition morph by default, swipe slides, zoom, and pull-to-dismiss.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @ramka/svelte
```

Peer dependency: `svelte` >= 5.40. Works in SvelteKit and plain Vite apps.

## Quick start

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { items }: { items: { id: string; src: string; thumb: string; alt: string; caption?: string }[] } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  {#each items as item, i (item.id)}
    <Lightbox.Trigger index={i}>
      <img src={item.thumb} alt={item.alt} />
    </Lightbox.Trigger>
  {/each}

  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content aria-label="Photo viewer">
      <Lightbox.Slides aria-label="Photos" aria-roledescription="carousel">
        {#each items as item, i (item.id)}
          <Lightbox.Slide>
            <Lightbox.Item index={i} caption={item.caption ?? item.alt} aria-label="{i + 1} of {items.length}">
              <Lightbox.Zoom>
                <Lightbox.Media>
                  <img src={item.src} alt={item.alt} />
                </Lightbox.Media>
              </Lightbox.Zoom>
            </Lightbox.Item>
          </Lightbox.Slide>
        {/each}
      </Lightbox.Slides>

      <Lightbox.Counter />
      <Lightbox.ZoomOut aria-label="Zoom out" />
      <Lightbox.ZoomIn aria-label="Zoom in" />
      <Lightbox.Close aria-label="Close" />
      <Lightbox.Caption />
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

The trigger is a plain `<button>`; its first `img` is the morph source. Every string in the viewer is yours: the library ships none, so nothing it renders is ever in the wrong language.

ramka is free software under the [MIT License](https://ramka.dev/license) , for open-source and proprietary use.

## Coming from React?

This is the Svelte 5 port of [ramka](docs.md) by [Artur Bień](https://github.com/arturbien) . The parts and their names match [@ramka/react](docs/lightbox/api.md) one to one. What changes:

- No `render` prop. Render props become snippets, and refs such as `imageRef` and `morphRef` become attachments ( `&#123;@attach imageRef&#125;`).
- `bind:open` and `bind:index` replace `open` /`defaultOpen` and `value` /`defaultValue`.
- Counter’s snippet gets `&#123; current, total &#125;`. The caption type is exported as `CaptionContent`.
- Zoom takes `minZoom`, `maxZoom`, `zoomStep`, `scrollToZoom`, `wheelSensitivity`, `keyboardPanDistance`, `doubleClickDelay` and `onZoomChange`; `bind:this` exposes `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `zoomTo` and `reset`.
- ThumbnailStrip needs a ThumbnailStripTrack child around the thumbnails.
- React hooks become context getters: `getLightbox`, `getTrigger`, `getItem`, `getStage`.
- The morph and pull engines ship in one bundle instead of loading lazily.

## Next steps

- [Lightbox overview](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md) : guidelines and anatomy, then [Composition](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/composition.md).
- [Examples](docs/framework/svelte/examples/lightbox/photos-app.md) : live product demos and API pattern pages.

# Lightbox

Accessible primitives for fullscreen media lightboxes: compound Svelte components in the style of Bits UI. Cosmetically unstyled: you own colors, chrome, and radius values. ramka owns state, focus, gestures, morphs, and the structural styles those mechanics need.

## Usage guidelines

Work through these decisions in order:

1. **State**: uncontrolled, or `bind:open` and `bind:index`? See [State & lifecycle](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/state-lifecycle.md).
2. **Layout**: default to the swipe carousel ( [Slides + Zoom](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/composition.md#slides)). See [Composition](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/composition.md).
3. **Morph**: on by default. Wrap destination media in `Lightbox.Media`, put an `img` inside each Trigger, choose `crossfade` and `morphTo`, or pass `viewTransition=&#123;false&#125;` to opt out. See [View transitions](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/view-transitions.md).
4. **Gestures**: pull-to-dismiss on Content, Zoom on media, keyboard on Content. See [Gestures](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/gestures.md).
5. **Cosmetics vs mechanics**: colors, chrome, and radius *values* are yours. Structural styles (view-transition morph CSS, morph host box, zoom overflow, slide snap alignment) are applied by the library or through Media `width` /`height`. Slide track width (full-bleed or snug cards) is your CSS, see [Composition: Slides + Zoom](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/composition.md#slides). Style with the documented `data-*` attributes and CSS variables from the [API reference](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md).

## Anatomy

Import the namespace and compose parts. The sketch below is the default gallery shape (Slides + Zoom + chrome). Every part is optional except Root, which holds the state.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  <Lightbox.Trigger index={0}><img src="/thumb.jpg" alt="" /></Lightbox.Trigger>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        <Lightbox.Slide>
          <Lightbox.Item index={0}>
            <Lightbox.Zoom>
              <Lightbox.Media>
                <img src="/photo.jpg" alt="" />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Zoom>
          </Lightbox.Item>
        </Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
      <Lightbox.Counter />
      <Lightbox.ZoomOut aria-label="Zoom out" />
      <Lightbox.ZoomIn aria-label="Zoom in" />
      <Lightbox.Close aria-label="Close" />
      <Lightbox.Caption />
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

# State & lifecycle

Control open state and the active index with bindings, `createHandle()`, or both, and know when callbacks fire. Part of [Lightbox](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md).

## Controlled state

Bind `open` and `index` on [Root](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root) to drive the lightbox from URL params, a store, or sibling UI. Leave them unbound and Root keeps its own state, starting closed at index 0.

The React version splits this into `open` / `onOpenChange`, `value` / `onValueChange`, and `defaultOpen` / `defaultValue`. In Svelte, `bind:` covers all three: pass a plain value for the initial state, bind it to control it.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let open = $state(false);
  let index = $state(0);
</script>

<Lightbox.Root bind:open bind:index>
  <!-- triggers + content -->
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Imperative API

[Lightbox.createHandle()](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root) lets Triggers and Root live apart: pass the same handle to both. Call `open(index, &#123; triggerId &#125;)` from any button so the open still morphs from the matching [Trigger](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-trigger). The handle also has `close()`, `goTo(index)`, and a reactive `isOpen`.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { images }: { images: { id: string; src: string; alt: string }[] } = $props();
  const lightbox = Lightbox.createHandle();
</script>

<button type="button" onclick={() => lightbox.open(0, { triggerId: 'photo-0' })}>View gallery</button>

{#each images as img, i (img.id)}
  <Lightbox.Trigger handle={lightbox} id="photo-{i}" index={i}>
    <img src={img.src} alt={img.alt} />
  </Lightbox.Trigger>
{/each}

<Lightbox.Root handle={lightbox}>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        {#each images as img, i (img.id)}
          <Lightbox.Slide>
            <Lightbox.Item index={i}>
              <Lightbox.Zoom>
                <Lightbox.Media>
                  <img src={img.src} alt={img.alt} />
                </Lightbox.Media>
              </Lightbox.Zoom>
            </Lightbox.Item>
          </Lightbox.Slide>
        {/each}
      </Lightbox.Slides>
      <Lightbox.Close aria-label="Close" />
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

Inside one component you can skip the handle: `bind:this` on Root exposes `show(index)` and `close()`.

## Lifecycle callbacks

`onOpenChange` fires immediately when open flips: use it to sync the URL or external state. `onOpenChangeComplete` fires after enter and exit motion settles: use it for cleanup and focus. `onValueChange` reports the new index plus a [NavigationSource](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#types) (including `imperative` for handle navigation).

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { children } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root
  onOpenChange={(open) => console.log('sync URL or store', open)}
  onOpenChangeComplete={(open) => console.log('motion settled, clean up or move focus', open)}
  onValueChange={(index, { source }) => console.log(index, source)}
>
  {@render children()}
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## onBeforeOpen

When View Transitions are on, open is *prepare → optional image decode → optional onBeforeOpen → morph* . Use [Root](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root)’s `onBeforeOpen` to delay the morph until custom media is ready (iframe `load`, video, WebGL). It runs after the lightbox is mounted hidden, so destination nodes exist, and before `startViewTransition`.

Keep `awaitImageDecode` for photos (default `true`). For non-image destinations, pass `awaitImageDecode=&#123;false&#125;` and wait in `onBeforeOpen`. Bound your own timeout; `ctx.signal` aborts if a newer open or close wins. See [3D models](docs/framework/svelte/examples/lightbox/3d-models.md).

## onBeforeClose

`onBeforeClose` fires synchronously when close begins and, with View Transitions, *before* the old snapshot is captured. Use it to freeze custom media ( `video.pause()`, stop a rAF loop) so the close morph isn’t a mid-frame. Unlike `onBeforeOpen`, it cannot delay close. `onOpenChange(false)` is too late for this: it runs inside the transition callback, after the snapshot.

# Composition

Default to Slides + Zoom (swipe carousel with pinch zoom), size media to fill Content, then layer chrome. Part of [Lightbox](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md).

## Slides + Zoom

Prefer [Slides](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-slides) + [Slide](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-slide) for a swipeable snap carousel wired to the active index. Nearly every docs demo and example uses this layout. Slide boxes stay mounted; `preload` gates heavy Item content.

- Nesting rule: put `Item` and [Zoom](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom) *inside* each `Slide`. Pull transforms the item, not the snap box.
- User flings set an internal scroll lock so pull-to-dismiss, zoom chrome, and discrete prev/next do not fight the carousel mid-gesture.
- Scroll-driven index changes report `onValueChange` with `source: 'scroll'`, see [NavigationSource](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#types).
- The Item snippet’s `active` is the current index (drive expensive work here). `visible` means the item is in the preload window: use it for lightweight prefetch, not video autoplay.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { items }: { items: { id: string; src: string; alt: string }[] } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides preload={1}>
        {#each items as item, i (item.id)}
          <Lightbox.Slide>
            <Lightbox.Item index={i}>
              <Lightbox.Zoom>
                <Lightbox.Media>
                  <img src={item.src} alt={item.alt} />
                </Lightbox.Media>
              </Lightbox.Zoom>
            </Lightbox.Item>
          </Lightbox.Slide>
        {/each}
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

```css Slide track (full-bleed carousel)
[data-ramka-slide] {
  flex: 0 0 100%;
  min-width: 100%;
}
```

## Media layout

ramka is *cosmetically* unstyled (colors and chrome are yours), but Media may apply *structural* fit-box styles through `width` /`height` so the morph target has a correct aspect before pixels load. Slide width is your CSS too: [Slide](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-slide) only bakes in snap alignment ( `scroll-snap-align: center`, `scroll-snap-stop: always`); you size each snap box. For a full-bleed carousel, use `flex: 0 0 100%` and `min-width: 100%` on each slide (see the snippet above). Snug, variable-width tracks use a different width formula, see the [Default preset](docs/framework/svelte/presets/default.md). Item and Zoom fill the slide content box; size the stack so when Zoom scales past 1× the image can cover the viewport and is not clipped by a shorter ancestor.

- `Content`: fullscreen surface (`fixed inset-0` or a full dialog)
- `Slides`: `flex-1` (or an equivalent stretch)
- `Slide`: `flex: 0 0 100%; min-width: 100%` for a full-bleed track; `h-full` for height; put chrome and safe-area insets here as padding (not on Zoom)
- `Item`: already fills the Slide ( `width/height: 100%`)
- `Zoom`: already fills and centers (structural)
- `Media`: sized fit-box (morph and placeholder host); `<img>` or `<video>` inside

Keep Close, Counter, Caption, and thumbnails as *absolutely positioned siblings* of Slides (see Chrome below), not in-flow above or below Zoom. Resting insets belong on Slide padding and safe-area so zoomed media can still paint into that padding under chrome. Gesture details live in [Gestures](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/gestures.md).

Set HTML `width` and `height` on the destination `<img>` (from known pixel dimensions or CMS metadata) so the box and aspect ratio exist *before* pixels load. That avoids layout shift, keeps the morph target sized on slow networks, and prevents an unloaded image from collapsing to 0×0 (which can skip or weaken the open morph). When dimensions are unknown, see [URL-synced state](docs/framework/svelte/examples/lightbox/url-synced-state.md). For mixed media (photos plus WebGL) with [onBeforeOpen](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root) preheat, see [3D models](docs/framework/svelte/examples/lightbox/3d-models.md).

To fill the maximum available space without distorting the source aspect ratio, nest Media under [Lightbox.Zoom](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom) (a size container for `cqw` /`cqh`) and pass `width` /`height` to [Lightbox.Media](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-media). Media applies the inscribed fit-box ( `min(100cqw, 100cqh × w/h)` + `aspect-ratio: w / h`). Or put HTML `width` / `height` on the child image and omit the Media props: Media derives the box. When the box matches the source aspect, child `object-fit` is a no-op and Media’s grid stretch fills the box. Put border-radius on Media (the morph target). Leave chrome outside Media.

```svelte Viewer.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { src, alt, width, height }: { src: string; alt: string; width: number; height: number } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content class="fixed inset-0 flex flex-col">
      <Lightbox.Slides class="flex-1">
        <Lightbox.Slide class="h-full p-8">
          <Lightbox.Item index={0}>
            <Lightbox.Zoom>
              <Lightbox.Media {width} {height}>
                <img {width} {height} {src} {alt} />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Zoom>
          </Lightbox.Item>
        </Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

Live compositions: [Default preset](docs/framework/svelte/presets/default.md), [Twitter preset](docs/framework/svelte/presets/twitter.md), [Stories preset](docs/framework/svelte/presets/stories.md), [Photos app](docs/framework/svelte/examples/lightbox/photos-app.md).

## Stage (split layouts)

Use [Lightbox.Stage](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-stage) when Content holds more than the media pane, for example a thread sidebar beside the gallery. Stage is the media interaction surface: trackpad wheel pull-to-dismiss, Zoom pan cover geometry, and / Home / End gallery navigation are scoped to it. Content remains the dialog shell (focus trap, Esc, zoom shortcuts). Place side panels as siblings of Stage under Content so they keep native scroll and their own keyboard behavior. Without a Stage, Content itself is the stage (default full-bleed viewers need no change).

```svelte Stage + side panel
<Lightbox.Content aria-label="Post">
  <Lightbox.Stage class="media-pane">
    <Lightbox.Close aria-label="Close" />
    <Lightbox.Slides><!-- media --></Lightbox.Slides>
    <Lightbox.Previous aria-label="Previous" />
    <Lightbox.Next aria-label="Next" />
  </Lightbox.Stage>
  <aside><!-- thread / details --></aside>
</Lightbox.Content>
```

Attach Stage’s `morphRef` when the open and close morph should capture the Stage surface (or a descendant) instead of the active item: a 9:16 stories frame, the slides track, or a custom bezel. Decode and the thumbnail placeholder stay on the item. In Svelte, `morphRef` is an attachment: `&#123;@attach morphRef&#125;`.

```svelte Stage morphRef
<Lightbox.Stage>
  {#snippet children({ morphRef })}
    <div class="frame" {@attach morphRef}>
      <Lightbox.Slides><!-- media --></Lightbox.Slides>
    </div>
  {/snippet}
</Lightbox.Stage>
```

Live examples: [Twitter preset](docs/framework/svelte/presets/twitter.md), [Stories preset](docs/framework/svelte/presets/stories.md).

## Chrome

The site default viewer is Slides + Zoom with Counter, Close, ZoomIn and ZoomOut, Caption, and a desktop [ThumbnailStrip](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-thumbnail-strip) (scroll-linked midline track) as siblings inside [Content](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-content). Midline selection chrome goes in the strip’s `indicator` snippet. Thumbnails register by `index` like Triggers. Put Backdrop and Content in [Portal](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-portal). Stacking follows the usual dialog pattern: `isolation: isolate` on the app layout root and, with `keepMounted`, your own `z-index` on the Portal host (for example `class="relative z-[1]"`). Inside the portal, document order keeps Backdrop under Content.

Thumbnails go inside a [ThumbnailStripTrack](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-thumbnail-strip-track), the `role="tablist"` that the strip moves. Label the track, not the strip.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { items }: { items: { id: string; src: string; thumb: string; alt: string; caption: string }[] } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        {#each items as item, i (item.id)}
          <Lightbox.Slide>
            <Lightbox.Item index={i} caption={item.caption}>
              <Lightbox.Zoom>
                <Lightbox.Media>
                  <img src={item.src} alt={item.alt} />
                </Lightbox.Media>
              </Lightbox.Zoom>
            </Lightbox.Item>
          </Lightbox.Slide>
        {/each}
      </Lightbox.Slides>

      <Lightbox.Counter />
      <Lightbox.ZoomOut aria-label="Zoom out" />
      <Lightbox.ZoomIn aria-label="Zoom in" />
      <Lightbox.Close aria-label="Close" />

      <Lightbox.Caption />
      <Lightbox.ThumbnailStrip>
        <Lightbox.ThumbnailStripTrack aria-label="Photo thumbnails">
          {#each items as item, i (item.id)}
            <Lightbox.Thumbnail index={i}>
              <img src={item.thumb} alt="" />
            </Lightbox.Thumbnail>
          {/each}
        </Lightbox.ThumbnailStripTrack>
        {#snippet indicator()}
          <span aria-hidden="true"></span>
        {/snippet}
      </Lightbox.ThumbnailStrip>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

Packaged as a skin: [Default preset](docs/framework/svelte/presets/default.md).

## Dynamic item count

Items register on mount, and the item count comes from the registered items. Indices do not need to be contiguous, but Counter, loop edges, and preload distance all use that count. Prefer dense `0…n-1` indexes unless you leave holes on purpose. Before the viewer has mounted (for a counter outside it, say), Root’s `count` prop stands in.

# SvelteKit images

Use blurred placeholders (LQIP) with ramka. Lightbox-side blur depends on whether that item has a trigger image. Part of [Lightbox](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md).

The demos on this page delay every full-size lightbox image by about 500ms and bypass the browser cache on each open, so you can watch the placeholder mechanisms work on every open, with no DevTools throttling.

## When to use a placeholder

SvelteKit has no built-in blur placeholder like `next/image`. The usual setup is a tiny image from your pipeline (`vite-imagetools`, `sharp` at build time, or your CDN) painted as the `background-image` of the `<img>` until the real pixels arrive. This page calls that the LQIP. `@sveltejs/enhanced-img` works too: its output is a plain `<img>`, so everything below applies.

Decide **per item index**, not per gallery. ramka paints an open bridge only when that index has a registered trigger image (`imageRef`).

| Image | LQIP | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image inside `Lightbox.Trigger` | Yes | A regular page image: the LQIP covers its own load. ramka never paints a placeholder here. |
| Image inside `Lightbox.Thumbnail` | Yes | Same as a trigger: a regular page image. ramka bridges only the destination media, never strip thumbnails, so the LQIP is the only thing covering the thumb’s own load. |
| Lightbox image, index *has* a trigger image (`imageRef`) | No | While the full-size image loads, ramka paints the trigger’s image (already decoded and on screen) onto a canvas *behind* the lightbox image. An LQIP background sits on the lightbox image itself, in front of that canvas, so it hides a sharp placeholder behind a blurry one. |
| Lightbox image, index has *no* trigger image | Yes | ramka has no trigger image to paint, so the LQIP is the only loading placeholder (see [No trigger image](#no-trigger-image)). |

**One exception:** pages that server-render the lightbox already open (deep links). The bridge is painted on gesture opens. A server-rendered open has no gesture, and before hydration nothing is decoded to paint from, while an LQIP is part of the server HTML itself. For those visits, destination blur is the only placeholder that can exist on first paint: enable it for the deep-link visit and keep destinations clean for regular visits (decide once per mount).

## Do

Use the same asset for trigger and destination. Put the LQIP on the trigger; leave the destination clean. A square trigger crop is CSS only: keep the source aspect matched to Media. See [View transitions: Source aspect](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/view-transitions.md#source-aspect) for a live Do / Don’t.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { photo }: { photo: { src: string; lqip: string; width: number; height: number } } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  <Lightbox.Trigger index={0}>
    {#snippet children({ imageRef })}
      <img
        {@attach imageRef}
        src={photo.src}
        alt="Mountain lake"
        class="aspect-square size-full bg-cover object-cover"
        style:background-image="url({photo.lqip})"
      />
    {/snippet}
  </Lightbox.Trigger>

  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        <Lightbox.Slide>
          <Lightbox.Item index={0}>
            <Lightbox.Zoom>
              <Lightbox.Media width={photo.width} height={photo.height}>
                <img src={photo.src} alt="Mountain lake" sizes="100vw" fetchpriority="high" />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Zoom>
          </Lightbox.Item>
        </Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Don’t

An LQIP on a lightbox image whose index has a trigger image covers ramka’s bridge with a blur while the full image loads.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<Lightbox.Media width={photo.width} height={photo.height}>
  <img
    src={photo.src}
    alt="Mountain lake"
    sizes="100vw"
    class="bg-cover"
    style:background-image="url({photo.lqip})"
  />
</Lightbox.Media>
```

## No trigger image

If an index has no trigger `imageRef`, ramka has nothing to paint. Use a destination LQIP for those items only, not for siblings that still have a trigger image.

### +N extras

Open the +N tile, then swipe past the triggered photos. Overflow slides show the LQIP; indexes 0 and 1 stay on ramka’s trigger-image bridge. Close uses [morphTo="closest"](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/view-transitions.md#morph-to).

```svelte Album.svelte
<Lightbox.Root morphTo="closest">
  {#each photos.slice(0, visible) as photo, i (photo.src)}
    <Lightbox.Trigger index={i} crossfade={i === visible - 1 ? 'both' : undefined}>
      {#snippet children({ imageRef })}
        <img {@attach imageRef} src={photo.src} alt="" class="bg-cover" style:background-image="url({photo.lqip})" />
      {/snippet}
    </Lightbox.Trigger>
  {/each}

  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        {#each photos as photo, i (photo.src)}
          <Lightbox.Slide>
            <Lightbox.Item index={i}>
              <Lightbox.Zoom>
                <Lightbox.Media width={photo.width} height={photo.height}>
                  <img
                    src={photo.src}
                    alt=""
                    sizes="100vw"
                    class="bg-cover"
                    style:background-image={i >= visible ? `url(${photo.lqip})` : undefined}
                  />
                </Lightbox.Media>
              </Lightbox.Zoom>
            </Lightbox.Item>
          </Lightbox.Slide>
        {/each}
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

### Non-image trigger

Initials and swatches have a Trigger but no trigger image. Blur on the lightbox image is the loading placeholder.

```svelte Team.svelte
<Lightbox.Root>
  {#each team as person, i (person.name)}
    <Lightbox.Trigger index={i} crossfade="both">
      <span style:background={person.color}>{person.initials}</span>
    </Lightbox.Trigger>
  {/each}

  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        {#each team as person, i (person.name)}
          <Lightbox.Slide>
            <Lightbox.Item index={i}>
              <Lightbox.Zoom>
                <Lightbox.Media width={person.photo.width} height={person.photo.height}>
                  <img
                    src={person.photo.src}
                    alt="Portrait of {person.name}"
                    class="bg-cover"
                    style:background-image="url({person.photo.lqip})"
                  />
                </Lightbox.Media>
              </Lightbox.Zoom>
            </Lightbox.Item>
          </Lightbox.Slide>
        {/each}
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Checklist

- Per index: trigger image means no destination LQIP; no trigger image means a destination LQIP is fine
- Match Media `width` /`height` to the image source aspect
- Trigger and destination must share that intrinsic aspect (CSS-crop the tile; don’t serve a differently cropped file). See [Source aspect](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/view-transitions.md#source-aspect)
- Trigger: `imageRef` (or [getTrigger()](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#context)); an LQIP on the trigger image is fine
- `ThumbnailStrip` thumbs are regular images: an LQIP is fine, same as triggers
- Prefer `fetchpriority="high"` on the open destination. See [View transitions](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/view-transitions.md)
- `sizes="100vw"` for fullscreen
- Skip `size-full` on the image: Media already fills a direct img child

# View transitions

Morph open and close between a trigger and the active item with the browser View Transitions API. Part of [Lightbox](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md). Unsupported browsers, reduced motion, and low-end devices fall back to a plain fade.

## Morph refs

Morph is on by default (`viewTransition` on [Root](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root)). Pass `viewTransition=&#123;false&#125;` to opt out. Recommended destination shape: [Lightbox.Media](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-media) around the `<img>` or `<video>` (a sized fit-box that is both morph target and placeholder host). On [Trigger](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-trigger), the first `img` inside is the morph source on its own. To be explicit, take the refs from the children snippet; both are attachments:

- `imageRef`: attach to the Trigger thumb `<img>` whose pixels bridge the morph. Media finds the destination image (or video poster) by itself. Open reuses the already-decoded bitmap so the transition doesn’t flash empty space.
- `morphRef`: optional escape hatch when morph bounds should differ from Media or the image (tile with overlay, swatch + label).

Nested components can read the same refs from context with [getTrigger() and getItem()](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#context) instead of threading the snippet argument. Use `awaitImageDecode` on [Root](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root) when you want a short wait for the destination image before the morph starts (default cap about 200ms).

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { thumb, src }: { thumb: string; src: string } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root morphTo="active">
  <Lightbox.Trigger index={0}>
    {#snippet children({ imageRef })}
      <img {@attach imageRef} src={thumb} alt="" />
    {/snippet}
  </Lightbox.Trigger>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        <Lightbox.Slide>
          <Lightbox.Item index={0}>
            <Lightbox.Zoom>
              <Lightbox.Media>
                <img {src} alt="" />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Zoom>
          </Lightbox.Item>
        </Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Source aspect

The morph snapshots whatever pixels are on the trigger `<img>` and interpolates them into the destination Media box. That only looks like one photo when both sides share the *same intrinsic aspect ratio*: the same file, or srcset candidates of that file. A square tile is fine; crop it with CSS (`object-fit: cover`), not by baking `w=h&fit=crop` into a different image.

A CDN-cropped 1∶1 thumb against a 3∶2 lightbox image will reframe mid-animation: ramka paints the square thumb into the landscape box, then the full file lands with a different crop. Element boxes may differ. Intrinsic aspect must not.

These demos delay the lightbox image by about 500ms so the handoff is visible on every open.

```svelte Do.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { photo }: { photo: { src: string; width: number; height: number } } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  <Lightbox.Trigger index={0}>
    {#snippet children({ imageRef })}
      <img {@attach imageRef} src={photo.src} alt="Mountain lake" class="aspect-square size-full object-cover" />
    {/snippet}
  </Lightbox.Trigger>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        <Lightbox.Slide>
          <Lightbox.Item index={0}>
            <Lightbox.Zoom>
              <Lightbox.Media width={photo.width} height={photo.height}>
                <img src={photo.src} width={photo.width} height={photo.height} alt="Mountain lake" />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Zoom>
          </Lightbox.Item>
        </Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

```svelte Dont.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { photo, squareThumb }: { photo: { src: string; width: number; height: number }; squareThumb: string } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  <Lightbox.Trigger index={0}>
    {#snippet children({ imageRef })}
      <!-- ✗ a 1∶1 file; Media below is the full 3∶2 photo -->
      <img {@attach imageRef} src={squareThumb} alt="Mountain lake" class="size-full object-cover" />
    {/snippet}
  </Lightbox.Trigger>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        <Lightbox.Slide>
          <Lightbox.Item index={0}>
            <Lightbox.Zoom>
              <Lightbox.Media width={photo.width} height={photo.height}>
                <img src={photo.src} width={photo.width} height={photo.height} alt="Mountain lake" />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Zoom>
          </Lightbox.Item>
        </Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Trigger crossfade

Controls whether the morph *dissolves* between trigger and item snapshots or hard-cuts geometry only.

- **Omit (default)**: hard-cut. Best when trigger and item show the *same* picture at the *same intrinsic aspect* (a CSS `object-cover` window or a smaller srcset is fine; a CDN-baked crop that changes the aspect is not, see [Source aspect](#source-aspect)). Leaves `data-ramka-crossfade` unset on `<html>` during the transition.
- `both`: dissolve on open and close (stack → single photo, +N overlay tile).
- `open` / `close`: dissolve in one direction only (poster → live video often wants `close`).

Keep trigger and item images on `object-fit: cover` (or the same fit) so crops stay coherent. Put border-radius on the morph target itself: the library interpolates `--lightbox-morph-border-radius-from/to` on `<html>`.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { photo, extras }: { photo: string; extras: number } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root morphTo="closest">
  <Lightbox.Trigger index={0} crossfade="both">
    {#snippet children({ imageRef })}
      <div class="relative">
        <img {@attach imageRef} src={photo} alt="" />
        <span>+{extras}</span>
      </div>
    {/snippet}
  </Lightbox.Trigger>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        <Lightbox.Slide>
          <Lightbox.Item index={0}>
            {#snippet children({ imageRef })}
              <img {@attach imageRef} src={photo} alt="" />
            {/snippet}
          </Lightbox.Item>
        </Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Root morphTo

Picks which trigger receives the *close* morph:

- `active` (default): the trigger for the current active index. No morph if that index has no trigger.
- `origin`: always the trigger that opened the lightbox (one tile opens many items).
- `closest`: the active index if registered, otherwise the nearest registered trigger.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';
</script>

<Lightbox.Root morphTo="closest">
  <Lightbox.Trigger index={0}><!-- first thumb --></Lightbox.Trigger>
  <Lightbox.Trigger index={1}><!-- +N tile --></Lightbox.Trigger>
  <!-- items 2…n close to the nearest trigger -->
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        <Lightbox.Slide><Lightbox.Item index={0} /></Lightbox.Slide>
        <Lightbox.Slide><Lightbox.Item index={1} /></Lightbox.Slide>
        <Lightbox.Slide><Lightbox.Item index={2} /></Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Root scrollTriggerIntoView

When the page scrolls while the lightbox is open, the close morph can land off-screen. Use `scrollTriggerIntoView` to keep the target trigger in view:

- `onChange`: scroll to the active trigger as the index changes (preemptive).
- `onOpenComplete`: reposition once open settles (invisible under the overlay; `instant` recommended).
- `onClose`: scroll just before the close morph (visible jump at close start).

Pass one option or an array. Each option also accepts `block` / `inline` alignment (default `nearest`): use `inline: 'center'` for horizontal snap strips with variable-width tiles. Pair with `morphTo` so the scrolled element is the same one that receives the morph.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<Lightbox.Root
  scrollTriggerIntoView={[
    { type: 'onChange', behavior: 'instant' },
    { type: 'onOpenComplete', behavior: 'instant' }
  ]}
>
  <!-- triggers + content -->
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Programmatic open

Prefer [createHandle()](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root): `open(index, &#123; triggerId &#125;)` associates a Trigger that declared that `id` so the open morph can use that element. Without a registered trigger (or `triggerId`), the open falls back to the fade path. Trigger clicks still morph. Demo: [State & lifecycle: Imperative API](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/state-lifecycle.md#imperative).

## Styling

You write **zero** view-transition CSS: the library injects the structural `::view-transition-*` rules itself (see [Injected CSS](#injected-css)) and writes document hooks during a morph so your own skin CSS can react, for example to keep Backdrop and Content fades on the morph’s clock. Attribute and CSS variable tables live under [Document (view transitions)](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-view-transition-document). Hooks:

- `data-ramka-view-transition`: `opening` | `closing`
- `data-ramka-crossfade`: dissolve path (present when Trigger `crossfade` is active for this phase; absent for hard-cut)
- `--lightbox-morph-border-radius-from/to`, `--lightbox-morph-old/new-opacity`
- `data-ramka-vt-preset`, `--lightbox-vt-duration`, `--lightbox-vt-easing`, `--lightbox-vt-crossfade-close-easing`, `--lightbox-vt-root-easing`: the active timing preset, written by the library (see [Timing presets](#timing-presets))
- [Trigger](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-trigger) `data-morph-target` / [Item](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-item) `data-skip-fade`: hide the live morph source and suppress entrance fades on the destination while the transition layer is up

Motion splits into **timing** (a preset picked on Root, see below) and **structure** (injected by the library). Your CSS only handles cosmetics, and reads the library-written variables where it wants to stay in sync.

## Timing presets

Morph duration and easing are chosen with the `viewTransition` prop on [Root](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root): pass a preset name instead of `true`:

- `"default"`: 360ms, sheet curve with a tamed launch (what `true` runs)
- `"snappy"`: 340ms, hotter launch; reads quicker
- `"relaxed"`: 400ms, softer launch and longer settle
- `"spring"`: 450ms, critically damped spring; Photos-style settle

```svelte Picking a preset
<Lightbox.Root viewTransition="spring"><!-- … --></Lightbox.Root>
```

Timing is preset-based rather than free-form CSS on purpose: each preset is vetted on-device to stay smooth and skip-safe on iOS Safari (including Low Power Mode) and Android, where arbitrary curves stutter or teleport. The library publishes the preset timing as `--lightbox-vt-duration` / `--lightbox-vt-easing` / `--lightbox-vt-root-easing` in two places: always on the [Portal](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-portal) host, and, together with `data-ramka-vt-preset`, on `documentElement` for the duration of a morph. Read those variables in your own CSS as the skin’s single motion clock (for example `transition: opacity var(--lightbox-vt-duration, 360ms) ease-out` on Backdrop and Content): during a morph the fades stay in lockstep with it, and on the non-morph paths (unsupported browsers, reduced motion, low-end fallback) they still run on the preset’s timing. Do not set the variables yourself.

## Injected CSS

On first [Root](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root) mount the library injects one stylesheet with everything a morph structurally needs: no copy-paste block to maintain, and several skins on one page can never fight over it.

- **Name isolation**: `startViewTransition` snapshots the whole document, so any page element with its own `view-transition-name` would paint *over* the lightbox. Every name is cleared while `data-ramka-view-transition` is set; the morph target re-applies its name inline with `!important` and stays the only captured group.
- **Morph group**: clipping and border-radius interpolation (put radius on the morph target element; the library writes `--lightbox-morph-border-radius-from/to`), timed by the active preset.
- **Snapshots**: hard-cut by default (`object-fit: cover`, no browser dissolve). When Trigger `crossfade` sets `data-ramka-crossfade`, the dissolve path (browser fade, `plus-lighter`, `object-fit: fill`) runs on the same preset clock, on a shorter window so the outgoing snapshot is gone before the size settles.
- **Root snapshot**: the page-behind crossfade, kept as a *single* root group (promoting Backdrop or Content into named groups tanks Safari). Fade scrim and chrome with live `opacity` transitions instead.
- **Morph-target hide**: `[data-morph-target]` gets `opacity: 0` with a 200ms fade-back (disabled during the transition so it can’t be captured mid-flight), so the live trigger never shows doubled under the morphing snapshot.
- **Thumb-jump crossfade**: the element-scoped Slides transition started when a ThumbnailStrip thumbnail jumps several slides, tunable with `--lightbox-select-vt-duration/easing` on Slides.

Everything except name isolation is gated under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`. The stylesheet is inserted at the *start* of `<head>`, so your own stylesheets cascade after it: overriding an injected rule takes an ordinary declaration of equal specificity, no `!important` needed.

Lifecycle timing for your own CSS: Content and Backdrop stay mounted through exit animations; while a morph open is preparing they may be `visibility: hidden` so the morph layer owns the pixels. Prefer `onOpenChangeComplete` for post-motion work, see [State & lifecycle: Lifecycle callbacks](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/state-lifecycle.md#lifecycle).

# Gestures

Pull-to-dismiss, zoom and pan, and keyboard ownership. Part of [Lightbox](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md). For the usual gallery chrome (pull, zoom, keyboard) see the [Default preset](docs/framework/svelte/presets/default.md).

## Content pullToClose

Content enables pull-to-dismiss by default (`pullToClose`). Drag down (touch) or wheel-dismiss (trackpad) scales the surface and sets `data-pulling` / `data-pull-dismissing` plus `--lightbox-pull-progress` (0→1).

- The hit target is Stage-wide (or Content when Stage is omitted): letterbox and empty Stage area can start a pull, matching the trackpad wheel. Interactive controls (buttons, links, inputs, `[data-ramka-no-pull]`) keep their press. Side panels outside Stage do not start a pull.
- Disabled while zoomed above 1×, and while Slides is scrolling until `scrollend` (so a gallery swipe that turns vertical cannot pull mid-gesture).
- Backdrop is optional. When used, nest it inside [Portal](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-portal) beside Content. Pull still works without a Backdrop.

Open and close fades are plain CSS on your Backdrop and Content classes, keyed to `data-open` and `@starting-style`. Pull then modulates the open scrim (media stays opaque) through `--lightbox-pull-progress`.

When a pull is released short of the threshold, the surface springs back and the library publishes `--lightbox-pull-snap-duration` / `--lightbox-pull-snap-easing` for the duration of that spring. Reference them in your `transition` (with your open and close values as the fallbacks, as below) and anything keyed to `--lightbox-pull-progress` (backdrop opacity, chrome, blur) eases back on the same curve and duration as the item.

```css Open / close CSS
.lightbox-backdrop {
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity var(--lightbox-pull-snap-duration, var(--lightbox-vt-duration, 360ms))
    var(--lightbox-pull-snap-easing, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1));
}

@starting-style {
  .lightbox-backdrop[data-open] {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}

.lightbox-content {
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity var(--lightbox-vt-duration, 360ms) cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
}

.lightbox-content[data-open] {
  opacity: 1;
}

@starting-style {
  .lightbox-content[data-open] {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

```css Pull progress CSS
.lightbox-backdrop[data-open] {
  opacity: calc(1 - var(--lightbox-pull-progress, 0) * 0.6);
}

.lightbox-backdrop[data-pulling] {
  transition: none;
}

.lightbox-chrome {
  opacity: 1;
  visibility: visible;
  transition:
    opacity 200ms,
    visibility 0s linear 0s;
}

.lightbox-content:is([data-pulling], [data-pull-dismissing]) .lightbox-chrome {
  opacity: 0;
  visibility: hidden;
  transition:
    opacity 200ms,
    visibility 0s linear 200ms;
}
```

## Zoom

Wrap media in [Zoom](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom) (inside Item, typically inside Slide). Prefer [Media](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-media) inside Zoom so pan and `maxZoom` use the sized content box. Supports pinch, pan, double-tap, ctrl/meta+wheel (or `scrollToZoom`), and keyboard pan when focused.

Zoomed media can cover the full Content surface only if Slide → Item → Zoom → Media fill that box, see [Composition: Media layout](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/composition.md#media-layout).

[ZoomIn](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-in) / [ZoomOut](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-out) can sit in toolbar chrome outside Zoom: they target the *active* slide through Root’s active-zoom bridge. Content reflects `data-zooming` / `data-zoomed` for styling.

```svelte Viewer.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { src, alt }: { src: string; alt: string } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root>
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content>
      <!-- toolbar chrome, targets the active slide's Zoom -->
      <Lightbox.ZoomOut aria-label="Zoom out" />
      <Lightbox.ZoomIn aria-label="Zoom in" />
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        <Lightbox.Slide>
          <Lightbox.Item index={0}>
            <Lightbox.Zoom>
              <Lightbox.Media>
                <img {src} {alt} />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Zoom>
          </Lightbox.Item>
        </Lightbox.Slide>
      </Lightbox.Slides>
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Keyboard & focus

[Content](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-content) is the keyboard authority while open:

- Esc: close
- : pan when zoomed, otherwise previous and next
- / / 0: zoom in, out, reset (active Zoom)

Image zoom uses unmodified keys only: / Ctrl and the other modified combos are left to the browser, so page zoom (WCAG 1.4.4 text resize) keeps working while the dialog is open.

Focus is trapped in the dialog; closing restores focus to the opening Trigger. Native page pinch-zoom is blocked while Content is mounted so it does not fight `Lightbox.Zoom`.

## Interaction matrix

| State | Pull | Zoom chrome / buttons | Prev / Next |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Idle, zoom = 1 | Allowed | Allowed | Allowed |
| Zoomed > 1 | Blocked | Allowed | Arrows pan; buttons still navigate |
| Slides flinging | Blocked | Blocked | Blocked until settle |
| Pulling | Active | Should idle | Should idle |

# Zoom & a11y

How ramka’s zoom and pan, on desktop and on touch, line up with mainstream image viewers, and how they map to WCAG 2.2. For the wiring and gesture ownership, see [Gestures](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/gestures.md).

## Desktop conventions

Desktop image viewers split into two families, depending on whether the surface is treated as a *media viewer* or a *canvas / document*:

- **Media-viewer model** (Google Photos, Lightroom, PhotoSwipe, OpenSeadragon): a bare scroll wheel zooms toward the cursor; drag pans.
- **Canvas / document model** (Figma, macOS Preview, Google Maps on trackpad): a bare scroll pans, and zoom is gated behind a modifier (Ctrl / ) or a trackpad pinch, so it never hijacks the user’s scroll.

Regardless of family, four things are near-universal: **drag pans** when zoomed, **wheel/pinch zoom is focal** (zooms toward the pointer), **double-click toggles** zoom, and **Ctrl / +wheel and trackpad pinch always zoom** . The only real disagreement is whether a *bare* wheel zooms or pans.

| App | Bare scroll | Ctrl / +wheel · pinch | Double-click | Drag |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| macOS Preview | Pan / scroll | Zoom (pinch) | Smart-zoom toggle | Pan |
| Apple Photos (Mac) | n/a | Zoom (pinch) | Toggle 1×↔zoom | Pan |
| Windows Photos | Navigate | Zoom (Ctrl+wheel) | Toggle | Pan |
| Google Photos (web) | Zoom to cursor | Zoom | Toggle | Pan |
| Google Maps | Zoom to cursor | Zoom | Zoom-in step | Pan |
| PhotoSwipe v5 | Opt-in (wheelToZoom) | Zoom (pinch) | Toggle | Pan |
| OpenSeadragon | Zoom to cursor | Zoom | Zoom-in step | Pan |
| Lightroom | Zoom | Zoom | Toggle 1:1 | Pan |
| Figma / Miro (canvas) | Pan | Zoom to cursor | n/a | Pan (space) |

## ramka on desktop

ramka defaults to the canvas model: Ctrl / +wheel and trackpad pinch zoom to the cursor, a bare wheel is a no-op, and `scrollToZoom` on [Zoom](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom) opts into the media-viewer behavior. That is the more embed-friendly default: a lightbox often lives inside a scrollable page, so bare-wheel zoom risks trapping the user’s scroll.

The Svelte port differs from `@ramka/react` in two rows below: the bare wheel does not pan a zoomed image yet, and trackpad pinch is clamped at the zoom limits instead of rubber-banding past them.

| Interaction | ramka | Consensus | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Trackpad pinch | Zooms to cursor through ctrlKey+wheel; hard-clamped at min/max. Safari GestureEvent is only blocked from page zoom, not read | Zoom to cursor | Match, without rubber-band (port gap) |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel | Zooms, focal at cursor; hard-clamped at min/max | Zoom to cursor | Match |
| Bare scroll wheel | Off by default (scrollToZoom=false): no-op inside Zoom | Split: media viewers zoom, canvas apps pan | Defensible default; opt-in covers the other |
| Double-click | Toggles zoom, focal at cursor | Toggle, focal | Match |
| Drag to pan | Yes: grab / grabbing cursor, elastic plus momentum | Universal | Match |
| Wheel to pan (zoomed) | Not yet: a bare wheel does not pan | Common | Port gap |
| Zoom buttons | ZoomIn / ZoomOut, zoomStep ×2 | Common | Zooms about center, not cursor |
| Keyboard zoom | + = − _ and 0 to reset (⌘/Ctrl combos stay browser page zoom) | Expected | Match |
| Keyboard pan | Arrows pan (keyboardPanDistance, 50px) when zoomed | Expected | Match |
| Max zoom | Auto-capped to the image's native resolution (fallback 4×) | Best practice (avoids blur) | Better than many |
| Cursor at 1× | No zoom-in affordance (consumer CSS) | Some apps show a zoom-in cursor | Minor discoverability gap |

The one intentional inconsistency: [ZoomIn](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-in) / [ZoomOut](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-out) zoom about the center rather than the cursor. That is standard (buttons have no pointer position) and matches Google Maps / OpenSeadragon button behavior.

## Mobile conventions

Touch is far more uniform than desktop. Every mainstream photo viewer converges on the same model, set by iOS Photos and Android’s Google Photos:

- **Pinch to zoom**, focal at the pinch midpoint. The image stays glued to the centroid, so spreading and sliding two fingers zoom and pan as one gesture, with a *rubber-band* overshoot past the min/max that snaps back on release.
- **Double-tap** toggles between fit and a zoomed level, centered on the tap point.
- **One- or two-finger drag pans** while zoomed, with **inertia / momentum** on release.
- At fit, a **horizontal swipe navigates** and a **downward swipe dismisses** the viewer.

The subtle but critical part is arbitration: pinch, pan, swipe-to-navigate, and swipe-to-dismiss all start from the same finger, so a viewer has to decide which gesture owns a given touch without misfiring.

| App | Pinch | Double-tap | Pan | Momentum | Swipe down |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iOS Photos | Focal, rubber-band | Toggle at tap | 1-finger drag | Yes + overscroll | Dismiss |
| Android Google Photos | Focal, rubber-band | Toggle at tap | 1-finger drag | Yes | Dismiss |
| Instagram | Focal (peek), snaps back | Like (not zoom) | While pinched | No | Dismiss |
| Mobile Safari (page) | Focal | Toggle (smart) | 1-finger drag | Yes | n/a |
| PhotoSwipe (mobile) | Focal, rubber-band | Toggle at tap | 1-finger drag | Yes | Dismiss |
| Telegram / WhatsApp | Focal | Toggle at tap | 1-finger drag | Yes | Dismiss |

## ramka on mobile

ramka implements the iOS/Android touch model, including the arbitration details that make it feel native: a double-tap that commits on pointerup (so a flick that starts near the last tap never zooms by mistake), elastic overscroll on both pinch and pan, momentum with bound-clamping, and a haptic tick on snap-back. Pull-to-dismiss and zoom/pan share a [navigation lock](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/gestures.md#matrix) so an in-flight Slides fling can’t be hijacked mid-scroll.

| Interaction | ramka | Consensus | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pinch to zoom | Focal at pinch midpoint; image follows the centroid (pinch and pan together); elastic past bounds, snaps back with a haptic tick | Focal + rubber-band | Match |
| Double-tap | Toggles zoom, focal at tap; commit waits for pointerup so a flick never misfires | Toggle at tap | Match |
| 1-finger pan (zoomed) | Elastic drag; velocity tracked | Universal | Match |
| 2-finger pan (zoomed) | Centroid pans and scale follows finger distance from the first move (no recognizer slop) | iOS Photos / pinch-pan | Close; small jitter can nudge zoom |
| Release with velocity | Momentum pan (decelerates, clamps to bounds) | iOS/Android inertia | Match |
| Swipe left / right | Navigates via Slides snap carousel (only at 1×) | Navigate photos | Match |
| Swipe down | Pull-to-dismiss; blocked while zoomed > 1× | Dismiss | Match |
| touch-action | none when zoomed; pan-x at 1× (lets Slides and the page own the swipe) | Guard native gestures | Correct |
| Native page pinch-zoom | Suppressed while Content is open so it never fights Lightbox.Zoom | Prevent conflict | Match |
| Haptics | Light tick on snap-back (navigator.vibrate, Android only) | iOS rubber-band feel | Better than many |

The touch model is where ramka is strongest. It matches the platform viewers almost point for point and adds haptics that most web lightboxes skip (where the browser exposes them: `navigator.vibrate` does nothing on iOS). Instagram-style *pinch-to-peek* (zoom only holds while fingers are down, then springs back to fit) is a deliberate product choice, not the default; ramka keeps the zoom level after release like Photos, which is the right behavior for a general-purpose viewer.

## UX heuristics

- **Zoom to the cursor.** The single most important pointer-zoom heuristic. ramka honors it for wheel, pinch, and double-click.
- **Don’t hijack bare scroll by default.** Keeping `scrollToZoom` off is the safer default for embedded lightboxes; enable it for full-bleed, single-image viewers.
- **Signal zoomability at rest.** Consider a `zoom-in` cursor over the image at 1× so mouse-only users discover double-click and Ctrl-wheel zoom. ramka leaves this to your CSS: the [Zoom](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom) surface exposes `data-zoom` only while scaled past 1×. Set `cursor: zoom-in` on the class you pass to `Lightbox.Zoom`; ramka’s grab / grabbing cursor wins once scaled:

```css zoom.css
.my-zoom {
  cursor: zoom-in;
}
```

- **Never steal swipe-to-dismiss.** On touch, pan must only take over *after* the image is zoomed; at fit, the vertical swipe belongs to pull-to-dismiss and the horizontal swipe to navigation. ramka gates this with `touch-action` and the navigation lock.
- **Rubber-band, don’t hard-stop.** Elastic overscroll on pinch and pan (plus a haptic tick on snap-back) is what makes zoom feel native rather than mechanical.
- **Size touch controls for fingers.** Give [ZoomIn](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-in) / [ZoomOut](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-out) and [Close](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-close) a hit area of at least 44×44 px on touch (WCAG 2.5.8 asks for 24 px or more; 44 px is the platform norm).

## WCAG conformance

These are the WCAG 2.2 success criteria that govern zoom and pan. ramka ships the pointer and keyboard alternatives the criteria expect:

| Success criterion | Level | Applies to | ramka |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2.5.1 Pointer Gestures](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-gestures.html) | A | Pinch (touch and trackpad) is a multipoint gesture and needs a single-pointer alternative. | **Pass.** Double-tap / double-click and the ZoomIn / ZoomOut buttons are all single-pointer. |
| [2.5.7 Dragging Movements](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html) | AA | Pan is drag-based and ramka implements its own pan, so the author-content clause applies. | **Partial.** Keyboard arrows pan, but a strict single-pointer, non-drag pan alternative (such as pan controls) is not built in. See the note below. |
| [2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html) | A | All zoom and pan must be reachable by keyboard. | **Pass.** +/−/0 and arrows route through the active-zoom bridge in Content. |
| [2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html) | AA | Zoom and close controls should be at least 24×24 CSS px (44 px is the touch norm). | **Consumer.** Sizing is your CSS in a headless library: a guidance item, not a library defect. |

**Note on 2.5.7.** Pan-by-drag has a keyboard alternative (arrows), which satisfies [2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html) , but 2.5.7 specifically wants a *single-pointer, non-drag* alternative, and keyboard does not count for it. If you must meet AA strictly, add pointer pan controls (such as edge or arrow buttons) alongside [ZoomIn](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-in) / [ZoomOut](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-out). Many shipping viewers do not either, but for enterprise targets it is worth flagging.

# RTL support

Run the lightbox in a right-to-left reading direction: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu. Part of [Lightbox](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md).

## Setting the direction

One prop. `dir="rtl"` on [Root](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root) mirrors the lightbox’s behavior (scroll geometry, arrow keys, thumbnail-strip travel) and is written to the [Portal](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-portal) host as a `dir` attribute, so CSS direction follows it too. That matters because the host mounts on `document.body`: a `dir` on your own layout wrapper would style the page and never reach the viewer.

Because the prop crosses the portal boundary on its own, it is also all you need to run a single RTL lightbox inside an otherwise LTR page: no wrapper element, no portal `container`. The demo further down this page does exactly that, since these docs are LTR.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { images }: { images: { id: string; src: string; alt: string }[] } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root dir="rtl">
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Backdrop />
    <Lightbox.Content aria-label="גלריית תמונות">
      <Lightbox.Slides>
        {#each images as img, i (img.id)}
          <Lightbox.Slide>
            <Lightbox.Item index={i}>
              <Lightbox.Media>
                <img src={img.src} alt={img.alt} />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Item>
          </Lightbox.Slide>
        {/each}
      </Lightbox.Slides>
      <Lightbox.Close aria-label="סגירה" />
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Already-RTL apps

If the whole app is RTL (`dir="rtl"` on `<html>`), you can omit the prop and the lightbox will still *look* right: nothing is written to the portal host when the prop is absent, so it inherits the document’s direction. Layout mirrors, and the page keeps control of it.

Pass the prop anyway. Behavior does not read your CSS, so it stays on its `'ltr'` default, and RTL layout with LTR behavior is the one misconfiguration with no visible symptom. The carousel still renders and still scrolls; it just resolves the wrong index for a scroll position, so the active marker and the visible slide drift apart. In development the library compares the two when Slides mounts and warns.

## What mirrors

Not everything flips, and the split is not arbitrary. Moving through an ordered list follows reading order, so it mirrors. Manipulating a surface directly (panning a zoomed photo, dragging a sheet away) does not: a drag follows your hand, and mirroring it would fight the gesture. The arrow keys serve both, which is why they mirror while navigating and stay physical while zoomed.

| Surface | Under RTL | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slide order & scroll | Mirrored | Index 0 sits at the inline-start (right) edge; the scroller runs right to left. |
| Horizontal arrow keys | Mirrored | ArrowLeft advances, ArrowRight goes back: travel follows reading order. |
| Home / End | Not mirrored | Home is always the first item, End the last. They address indices, not sides. |
| Thumbnail strip | Mirrored | Track, padding, and the active-thumb indicator all run on the inline axis. |
| Previous / Next | Mirrored position | Previous is the item nearer index 0, so it belongs on the inline-start side. |
| Zoomed panning | Not mirrored | Direct manipulation of a surface: ArrowRight pans right, as on a map. |
| Pull-to-dismiss | Not mirrored | The sheet follows your finger, which has no reading direction. |
| Morph / view transitions | Mirrored | The morph measures the trigger and the slide, so it follows whatever they do. |

## Indices never mirror

The imperative API is index-based, and indices are not sides. [createHandle()](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-create-handle)’s `open(3)` and `goTo(3)` land on the fourth item in either direction; what changes is that RTL renders it further left and the track travels the other way to reach it. The same holds for `bind:index` / `onValueChange` and for [Trigger](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-trigger)’s `index`.

The buttons inside the viewer below jump by index. Open it, then watch the strip: the photo you land on is the same one an LTR gallery would show.

```svelte Gallery.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';
  import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';

  let { children }: { children: Snippet } = $props();
  const lightbox = Lightbox.createHandle();
</script>

<button type="button" onclick={() => lightbox.open(0)}>פתיחת הגלריה</button>
<button type="button" onclick={() => lightbox.goTo(3)}>מעבר לתמונה 4</button>

<Lightbox.Root handle={lightbox} dir="rtl">
  {@render children()}
</Lightbox.Root>
```

## Styling for RTL

The library ships no styles, so mirroring your own chrome is your job, and logical properties do nearly all of it. Reach for `inset-inline-start` / `inset-inline-end` over `left` / `right`, `padding-inline` over `padding-left`, and `border-inline-start` for a divider beside a panel that changes sides. In Tailwind those are `start-*`, `end-*`, `ps-*`, `pe-*`, `ms-*`, and `text-start`. Every preset in this documentation is written this way.

Three things logical properties will not fix. Directional glyphs need flipping: `.nav:dir(rtl) svg &#123; transform: scaleX(-1); &#125;` turns a chevron around, since mirroring only the button’s position leaves it pointing the wrong way. Safe-area insets are physical, so pairing `inset-inline-start` with `env(safe-area-inset-left)` clears the notch on the wrong side; map them to the inline axis through a custom property that you swap under `:dir(rtl)`. And a counter like `1 / 7` is two digit runs around a neutral separator with nothing to anchor them, so an RTL base direction reorders it into `7 / 1`. Give [Counter](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-counter) `direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate;`.

## Copy is yours

Direction is only half of internationalization. The other half is words, and the library ships none of them: not a label, not a role description, not a slide name. A headless library cannot know your language, and a string baked into a primitive is copy you never approved: an English “carousel” announced inside Hebrew speech is worse than no announcement at all.

So every string a screen reader reads comes from you. Two of them are easy to miss because they are not visible on screen: `aria-roledescription` on [Slides](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-slides) and [Item](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-item), which replaces the word for the role, and the slide’s `aria-label`, which is where the [APG carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) puts the position, because a `group` cannot carry `aria-posinset`. A slide’s caption does not name it either, so a captioned slide with no label is still nameless. In development the library says so rather than letting it ship silently.

Add a thumbnail strip and the naming moves: each item becomes a `tabpanel` named by its thumbnail tab, so label the thumbnails and leave the items to inherit it.

```svelte Viewer.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let {
    items,
    t,
  }: {
    items: { id: string; src: string; alt: string }[];
    t: (key: string, vars?: Record<string, unknown>) => string;
  } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.Root dir="rtl">
  <Lightbox.Portal>
    <Lightbox.Content aria-label={t('viewer.dialog')}>
      <Lightbox.Slides aria-label={t('viewer.photos')} aria-roledescription={t('viewer.carousel')}>
        {#each items as item, i (item.id)}
          <Lightbox.Slide>
            <Lightbox.Item
              index={i}
              aria-roledescription={t('viewer.slide')}
              aria-label={t('viewer.position', { current: i + 1, total: items.length })}
            >
              <Lightbox.Media>
                <img src={item.src} alt={item.alt} />
              </Lightbox.Media>
            </Lightbox.Item>
          </Lightbox.Slide>
        {/each}
      </Lightbox.Slides>

      <Lightbox.Counter>
        {#snippet children({ current, total })}
          {t('viewer.position', { current, total })}
        {/snippet}
      </Lightbox.Counter>

      <Lightbox.Previous aria-label={t('viewer.previous')} />
      <Lightbox.Next aria-label={t('viewer.next')} />
      <Lightbox.Close aria-label={t('viewer.close')} />
    </Lightbox.Content>
  </Lightbox.Portal>
</Lightbox.Root>
```

# Content Security Policy

Running the lightbox on pages with a strict `style-src`. Part of [Lightbox](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md).

## What the library injects

The library is headless (your chrome, your CSS), but its structural rules have to come from somewhere. They live in one stylesheet with constant text. When the first Root or Trigger mounts, the library prepends it to `<head>` as a `<style data-ramka>` tag, so your own CSS still wins on equal specificity.

If a strict `style-src` refuses that tag, the library notices and delivers the same rules through a [constructed stylesheet](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CSSStyleSheet) instead, which CSP does not police at all. Everything keeps working with no configuration. The only thing a strict policy can cost is the first paint of a page that server-renders an *open* lightbox: that page carries the same tag inline so media fits, the active trigger hides, and the initial slide sits in place before any code runs. Refused, those first-paint details wait for hydration.

This differs from `@ramka/react`, which splits the rules across three tags and relies on React’s style hoisting. The Svelte port keeps one tag and one fallback.

## Passing a nonce

The standard way to allow specific inline styles is a [nonce](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/style-src#unsafe_inline_styles) : the server generates a random value per request, puts it in the header, and any `<style>` carrying the same value is allowed. Wrap [CSPProvider](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-csp-provider) around everything that renders lightbox parts and pass it that value; the library stamps it on the tag it inserts.

In SvelteKit, mint the nonce in `handle`, keep it on `event.locals` (declare `nonce: string` on `App.Locals`), and hand it to the root layout through a server load:

```typescript src/hooks.server.ts
import type { Handle } from '@sveltejs/kit';

export const handle: Handle = async ({ event, resolve }) => {
  const nonce = crypto.randomUUID();
  event.locals.nonce = nonce;
  const response = await resolve(event);
  response.headers.set(
    'Content-Security-Policy',
    `default-src 'self'; style-src-elem 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}'; style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline';`
  );
  return response;
};
```

```typescript src/routes/+layout.server.ts
import type { LayoutServerLoad } from './$types';

export const load: LayoutServerLoad = ({ locals }) => ({ nonce: locals.nonce });
```

```svelte src/routes/+layout.svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Lightbox } from '@ramka/svelte';

  let { data, children } = $props();
</script>

<Lightbox.CSPProvider nonce={data.nonce}>
  {@render children()}
</Lightbox.CSPProvider>
```

Put it above the *whole* app, not around one gallery. A detached [Trigger](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-trigger) living outside any Root reads the context too, and whichever part mounts first inserts the tag, so an uncovered Trigger would insert it without the nonce.

SvelteKit’s own `csp` option (with `mode: 'nonce'`) covers the scripts and styles Kit renders, but it does not hand its nonce to components. If you use it, either let your `handle` own the style directive as above, or rely on the constructed-stylesheet fallback.

## Server rendering

A Root that renders open on the server writes its tag straight into the HTML, nonce included, because Svelte components render their own markup. There is no framework call to thread the nonce through, so deep-linked pages that server-render an open viewer keep their first-paint styling under a strict policy. React needs the nonce passed to the render call as well, and Next.js does not forward it yet; that limit does not apply here.

Prerendered pages have no request to mint a nonce for. Use a hash-based policy for those (see below).

## Inline style attributes

Separate from `<style>` elements, CSP also governs `style="…"` attributes, and nonces cannot be applied to attributes at all. The library’s structural styles ride on inline attributes, which only matters for markup parsed from server HTML: styles set from JavaScript after hydration are not policed. If you server-render lightbox pages under a policy stricter than `style-src` alone, split the directives and keep `'unsafe-inline'` on the attribute half:

```tsx CSP header
Content-Security-Policy:
  default-src 'self';
  style-src-elem 'self' 'nonce-<generated-per-request>';
  style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline';
```

This is the industry-standard shape: Base UI and Material UI document the same split. Style *attributes* cannot exfiltrate data or execute code the way style elements can, so allowing them is a far smaller concession than `'unsafe-inline'` on elements.

## Hash-based policies

Statically hosted sites have no server to mint a per-request nonce. CSP’s alternative is a hash source: allow exactly this style block by its SHA-256. That is normally impractical for component libraries, but the library’s tag has *constant* text by design, so its hash is stable for a given release. The quickest way to collect it is the browser itself: load a page with the policy enforced and copy the `sha256-…` value Chrome prints in the console violation message into `style-src`. Collect it again when you upgrade the package, because the rule text can change between releases.

# API reference

Props, data attributes, and CSS variables for every [Lightbox](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox.md) part.

Each part spreads native attributes onto its element (listed as `...rest`). Custom props are listed below. Guides: [Composition](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/composition.md), [View transitions](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/view-transitions.md), [Gestures](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/gestures.md).

## By concern

- **State**: [Root](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root), [createHandle](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-create-handle)
- **Trigger / Item**: [Trigger](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-trigger), [Item](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-item), [Media](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-media)
- **Layout**: [Slides](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-slides), [Slide](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-slide)
- **View transitions**: [Root (VT props)](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-root), [Document (VT)](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-view-transition-document)
- **Shell**: [Portal](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-portal), [Backdrop](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-backdrop), [Content](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-content)
- **Gestures**: [Content](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-content), [Zoom](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom), [ZoomIn](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-in), [ZoomOut](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-zoom-out)
- **Chrome**: [Close](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-close), [Previous](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-previous), [Next](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-next), [Counter](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-counter), [Caption](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-caption), [ThumbnailGroup](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-thumbnail-group), [Thumbnail](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-thumbnail), [ThumbnailStrip](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-thumbnail-strip), [ThumbnailStripTrack](docs/framework/svelte/lightbox/api.md#api-thumbnail-strip-track)

### Root

Groups all parts of the lightbox and owns open state, active index, the view transition morph and the active zoom bridge. Renders no element of its own. Pass `handle` from `createHandle()` for imperative control and detached Triggers, or call `show(index)` and `close()` on the instance from `bind:this`. Prefer `onOpenChangeComplete` for work after the motion; use `scrollTriggerIntoView` so close morphs land on screen when the page scrolled while open.

#### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `Snippet` |  | Lightbox parts and page content (triggers typically live as children of Root). |
| handle | `LightboxHandle` |  | Imperative handle from `createHandle()`. Pass the same handle to detached `Lightbox.Trigger`s outside this Root. |
| open | `boolean` | `false` | Open state, bindable: use `bind:open` to read and write it, or pass a plain value for a one way initial state. Replaces React’s `open` / `defaultOpen` pair. |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when open state changes (immediately, before enter and exit animations finish). Prefer this for syncing URL state or stores. |
| onOpenChangeComplete | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the open or close transition settles. Receives `true` after open completes, `false` after close completes. Prefer this for cleanup and focus management. |
| index | `number` | `0` | Active index, bindable: use `bind:index` to read and write it. Replaces React’s `value` / `defaultValue` pair. |
| onValueChange | `(value: number, meta: { source: NavigationSource }) => void` |  | Callback when the active index changes, with the source of the navigation. |
| count | `number` |  | Total number of items, used until the mounted `Lightbox.Item`s have registered themselves. Items register when they mount in the browser, never during server rendering, so a page that server renders an open lightbox paints `Lightbox.Counter` as "n / 0" (and disables `Lightbox.Next` / `Lightbox.Previous` at the boundary when `loop` is off) until hydration. Pass the item total to make that first paint correct. Once any item mounts the live registry takes over and this prop is ignored. |
| loop | `boolean` | `false` | Wrap navigation at boundaries. |
| dir | `TextDirection` | `'ltr' (behavior); no `dir` attribute is written when omitted` | Reading direction. `'rtl'` mirrors slide navigation, thumbnail strip travel and the horizontal arrow keys (so `ArrowLeft` advances). The direction is written to the `Lightbox.Portal` host as a `dir` attribute, so CSS follows it across the portal boundary; that also runs one RTL lightbox inside an LTR page. Pass it whenever the surrounding UI is RTL: behavior falls back to `'ltr'` without it. In development `Lightbox.Slides` warns when its computed direction disagrees. |
| viewTransition | `boolean \| MorphPreset` | `true` | Morph between trigger and lightbox item through the View Transitions API. On by default: clicking a trigger morphs into the fullscreen item, and close morphs back. Pass `false` to open and close without a morph. Without View Transitions support or under `prefers-reduced-motion` the lightbox opens and closes without a morph. A preset name picks the motion: `'default'` (360ms, same as `true`), `'snappy'` (340ms, quicker launch), `'relaxed'` (400ms, softer settle) or `'spring'` (450ms, critically damped). The preset drives the morph, the crossfade and the root fade together. |
| scrollTriggerIntoView | `ScrollTriggerIntoView` | `null` | Scroll the trigger the close morph will land on into the viewport, so close animations stay on screen. Accepts one option or an array. Each option has a `type`: `'onChange'` scrolls whenever the active index changes while open, `'onOpenComplete'` scrolls once the open transition finishes (invisible under the viewer, `'instant'` recommended), `'onClose'` scrolls just before the close morph. `behavior` is `'smooth'` (default) or `'instant'`; `block` and `inline` are `scrollIntoView` alignments (`'nearest'` default). Respects `morphTo`. |
